unmapped_findings.value: For the Al-free reference alloy Fe-30Mn-1.2C (0 wt.% Al), the best mechanical behavior is in the as-homogenized state: 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS (high work hardening), and 77% TE. Aging leaves the YS virtually unchanged and slightly increases the hardness, but reduces UTS and TE. (The 360/830/77 values belong to the as-homogenized parent condition, not to the 600 °C/1 h aged sample; no exact numeric YS/UTS/TE values are reported in the text for the 600 °C/1 h aged condition of this alloy.)

source.reason: Qualitative embrittlement trend for the Al-free alloy upon aging.

unmapped_findings.value: Embrittlement of the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C); the 600 °C/1 h condition is a high-temperature but short-time aging treatment.

source.reason: Extracts the 0Al composition trends visible in Figure 3 that encompass the 600 °C/1 h condition.

unmapped_findings.value: In the RAP screening plots (Fig. 3), the 0Al Fe-30Mn-1.2C composition shows YS between roughly the 350 and 450 MPa lines (all aging conditions), UTS highest for the as-homogenised condition (above 800 MPa), TE highest for as-homogenised (~80%), and hardness nearly flat at ~200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al; the 600 °C/1 h (olive) curve lies within these bands at 0Al.

source.reason: Extracts the 0Al series trend from the strength-ductility summary plot.

unmapped_findings.value: In the tensile strength vs elongation plot (Fig. 4), the Al-free (0Al) Fe-30Mn-1.2C series follows the 'T + t' trend from about 490 MPa at ~8% elongation to about 800 MPa at ~70% elongation (annotation T: 1 h; T+t: 24 h).

source.reason: Al is needed for κ-carbide formation, so the 0 wt.% Al sample has no κ-carbide strengthening.

unmapped_findings.value: κ-carbides (L′1₂, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) require Al and form upon aging in Al-containing variants; the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample is not expected to contain κ-carbides, consistent with its single-phase austenite (SIMPLEX/TWIP) behavior.
